entity: the Vesuvius Challenge (scrollprize.org; also 'Scroll Prize'), which describes itself as an open science research organization reading the carbonized Herculaneum scrolls without unrolling them, created by Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross and Brent Seales and launched in 2023 as a global open competition with prizes for virtual unwrapping and ink detection on CT scans of the scrolls (prizes awarded by Scroll Prize, Inc.; EduceLab of the University of Kentucky its partner); formalized in the Revelation First meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-30 (https://www.revelationfirst.com/aggregators/vesuvius-challenge/)
row_type: C (a public entity on which the archive bears: an open research competition and organization reading the carbonized Herculaneum scrolls by machine; an entity of the Revelation First meta-aggregator)

classes_note: Three classes, each the census's own text object, intersection, method or evidence kind for the entity, stated by field sources at the loci given: (1) the Herculaneum papyri (census text_object, coverage; B1, B4, B12); (2) machine reading of ancient texts, virtual unwrapping and ink detection (census intersection 'ai-ancient-texts', evidence_kind 'machine reading, restoration or dating', method, unit, worked question 'machine-dating'; B1, B3, B4, B7, B12); (3) papyrological discovery, new texts recovered and what the papyrological record can contain (census intersection 'papyrology-discovery'; B3, B4, B7; the census's rf_intersection reads the entity here and is the archive's reading, ledgered as RF-, not a basis for admission by itself). The census's second evidence_kind, 'manuscript images', runs through class (2): the scans and renders are the images the field sources state. The Revelation First thesis (#202 and the deposits revelationfirst.com cites) bears on the entity only through class (3) and only where a sentence applies to papyri or papyrological evidence; the census's own does_not_answer ('anything on the New Testament: the Herculaneum library predates it and is not Christian') and the worked question's gap ('None of the four dates a New Testament papyrus or a composition') are ledgered as RF- claims. Aliases: the name, the domain and handle 'scrollprize', and 'Scroll Prize' (the census's aka; 'Scroll Prize, Inc.' is the prizes page's name for the awarding body). The bare 'Vesuvius' is not an alias (the volcano, the eruption of 79 AD); the 'Vesuvius' of #1443 Part X is the entity by context and is read at its paragraph. Admission by reading (§3.4): a bare mention, a reference-list entry or a keyword is not a claim.
